thread.title: Are Overbought Dow Stocks Stalling The Market's Rally?

author: Tom Aspray
title: Are Overbought Dow Stocks Stalling The Market's Rally?
text:
After a record-breaking performance by many of the market averages in August, things were not so easy after the Labor Day holiday. As expected, volume increased significantly, as traders had few excuses left to stay on vacation.
Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, U.S., on Friday, Aug. 31,2018 Photographer: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg
The defensive Dow Utility average was well-supported last week, up 1%. The Dow Jones Transports followed, with a 0.40% gain. The selling was the heaviest in the tech sector, as the Nasdaq 100 was down 2.9%, while the small-cap Russell 2000 lost 1.6% for the week. The S&P 500 lost 1%, closing lower all four days last week. The Dow Industrials were only down 0.20%.
There were warning signs before last week’s trading ( Should You Be Jumping Into Stocks Now? ) but now that the S&P 500 has declined 1.45% from its record high, should you be looking to buy?
In the analysis over the Labor Day weekend, I noted that Apple, Inc. (AAPL) had closed the month and week above its starc+ band. Those of you who are familiar with my starc band analysis know that when a market average, ETF, or stock closes above its starc+ band, it is in a high-risk buy area. Conversely, a close below the starc- band means it is a high-risk sell area. However, just because something closes at the starc- band does not prevent it from going even lower; it just means that the probabilities favor a move in the other direction.
In early May , I reviewed the five most oversold stocks in the Dow Industrials based on their close at the end of April. The most oversold was Pfizer (PFE), which now is up over 15% as of the August close. Of the five stocks, the average gain since my article has been 8.8%. Now, with the market correcting, I think there’s a lot to gain from paying attention to the Dow Industrials’ most over bought stocks.
From my end-of-August analysis, I noted that Apple, Inc. (AAPL) closed at $227.93 which was 2.22% above its monthly starc band. On the table, this is reflected as -2.2% since the column is calculated by taking the starc+ band reading and then subtracting the monthly closing price Tom Aspray-ViperReport.com
TomAspray-ViperReport.com
On the monthly chart, the arrows indicate the past four times since 2015 when AAPL has closed above its monthly starc+ band. The monthly relative performance (RS) has been above its WMA since December 2016, and turned up sharply this August. The monthly OBV has not been as strong, and just moved back above its WMA in August after being below it for June and July.
AAPL was down 2.8% last week, with the rising 20-day EMA at $217.87 and the monthly pivot at $217.94. These should be the support levels to watch before their new annual product launch this Wednesday. The 38.2% Fibonacci support is quite a bit lower at $210.69.
TomAspray-ViperReport.com
Pfizer (PFE) closed in August just 2.8% below its monthly starc+ band at $42.70. The monthly studies are positive for PFE and the weekly chart shows that it broke out of a trading range (lines a and b) in early August. PFE has closed above its weekly starc+ band for four of the past six weeks, but has not given up much ground over the past two weeks, and may just be pausing before another push to the upside.
The weekly studies look very positive, as the RS has been above its WMA since June 22, and broke out to the upside (line c) one week ahead of prices. The on-balance-volume (OBV) has been leading prices higher since April, when it moved through the resistance (line d).
TomAspray-ViperReport.com
Merck & Co. (MRK) is the other drug stock on the most overbought list, closing August just 3.9% below its monthly starc+ band. The weekly chart shows that it completed its trading range (lines a and b) five weeks ago. The height of the trading range has upside targets in the $80-area. The close on Friday was below the prior week’s doji low, generating a sell signal. There is good support at $65, which was the breakout level.
The downtrend in the RS has just slightly been overcome, so a pullback to its WMA is possible. The weekly OBV is above its WMA and therefore positive, but it is below the highs from 2017. The 20-day EMA and monthly pivot should provide support in the $67.90-$68.30 area.
So how are these overbought stocks likely to impact the market this week? Apple, Inc. (AAPL) is likely to have the most impact, as it is a 12.7% holding in the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and a 16% holding in the Technology Select Sector ETF (XLK). The good news is that the daily studies are positive for AAPL, so there are no signs yet of a top. A sharply higher close in AAPL could help to end the market’s correction.
TomAspray-ViperReport.com
The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) closed the week on its daily uptrend (line b) and the daily starc- band. The close was below the monthly pivot at $183.32, with monthly pivot support at $178.12. There is next good chart support (line a) at $177.95, with additional support at $174.27, the late July low.
The Nasdaq 100 A/D line has dropped below its still-rising WMA and is back to the July-August highs. The support at line d could be broken with another day or two of selling. The next important level to watch is the support at line e. The weekly A/D line (not shown) is still well above its rising WMA and positive.
TomAspray-ViperReport.com
The weekly chart of the Spyder Trust (SPY) shows the slightly lower close that was just above the monthly pivot at $287.07. There is further support in the $285.50 area with more important support at $284.21 and the January high. The rising 20-week EMA is at $278.95. A close above $290 should signal that the correction is over. The weekly starc+ band is at $295.10.
The weekly S&P 500 A/D line has turned down slightly, but is well above its rising WMA. The A/D line has more important support (line b). The weekly OBV made a new high with prices and only declined slightly last week.
The economic data was generally stronger than expected last week, especially the ISM Manufacturing Index which, at 61.3, was much better than the expected 57.7. The ISM Non-Manufacturing Index was also better than the consensus estimates. The slightly better-than-expected jobs report for September keep the odds high for a rate hike at the end of the month.
This week we have the latest readings on the Producer Price Index (PPI) and Consumer Price Index (CPI). Then on Friday, we have the Retail Sales, Industrial Production, and Consumer Sentiment.
It was a rough week for crude, as the November contract was down 2.6%, and Comex Gold lost another 0.5%, as the US dollar was slightly higher.
What to do? The monthly advance/decline lines for all the key markets made new highs in August. This was also the case for the weekly A/D lines, which points to a positive major and intermediate-term stock market trend. The daily A/D lines are in the corrective mode, so a further decline is possible this week.
Therefore, the current pullback is likely to be a buying opportunity, and we should know early in the week whether the correction is over, or if the major averages are going to test stronger support.
